reason: Host pressure's waiting reason embedded the live reading (e.g. 'CPU use (99% >= 80%)'). Queued chat turns, missions and harness turns save that text, so each change in the reading rewrote every waiting record (a real Core turn reached ~50 revisions in 17 minutes; up to one write and one queued stream frame per second) and widened stale-revision windows for harness and mission Stop. The reason now names only the metric and threshold. Selected: host load sampling/admission (with the new regression test), host pressure settings and admission, shared runtime capacity waits, Butler host-load reads, and the host-load-admission browser journey that shows the queued notice.
exclusions: test_butler_host_load.py::test_host_load_is_discoverable_read_only_and_rereads_core and test_host_cpu_budget.py (11 cases) fail identically on pristine origin/main and with this patch, so they are excluded. Playwright runs three of the eight host-load-admission profiles (desktop, Chromium 390, WebKit 390), all passing locally on the LAN origin; the other five are the same journey at other widths. Real-Core evidence (scratch Postgres Core, forced CPU threshold: a queued turn's revision 1 -> 33 in 40 s on main vs 2 -> 2 with this patch) is recorded in the PR, not executed by CI.
